notes:
`PRODUCT_VERSION` 1.1.0 · `CONTRACT_VERSION` 4.3.0

1.1.0 is about Cursor becoming a harness you can put real work on, and about the model field no longer being a release gate. Cursor arrives as the fourth provider with its own doctor check, usage meter, published rates and one-click MCP install, and two fixes later in the cycle made its read-only sessions both able to run and genuinely read-only. Every harness's model slug is now an open string, so a vendor shipping a model costs no toryo release. And an idea's impact is read off the idea's own text rather than off how often it has been re-filed, which is what makes the backlog rank again.

### Added

- **Cursor is toryo's fourth harness.** `cursor` is a provider everywhere the other three are: each of `code-task`'s five roles, a sequence `llm` block, `dispatch_enqueue`, board's pickers, and a `--provider-cursor` toggle beside the rest. `foreman doctor` gains a `cursor` check at `recommended` severity, so a Claude-only host is not reported broken. It probes both binary names an install carries, `cursor-agent` and `agent`, and appends the installed version, because Cursor's auto-update cannot be disabled and every capability claim toryo makes is scoped to a build. A cursor session is seeded the same resolved directive stack every other harness receives. It rides the prompt positional, since Cursor has no system-prompt flag, and the delivery audit now reports a file as partial when the stack outgrows what one command argument can carry, on cursor and claude alike. Cursor is also the first non-Claude harness with native tool policy: its own rule engine enforces the deny set and its stream names the matched command, so toryo supplies a spelling map rather than an emulation. Nothing is written into the repository under review; config, transcripts and MCP each have their own seam.
- **Cursor and Copilot both report usage now.** Cursor's meter is included spend over the plan's limit, in cents, resetting at the billing cycle end, with an on-demand meter and headroom for an account that sets a spend cap. Cursor publishes no personal usage API, so this reads the undocumented endpoint its own dashboard calls with the operator's session token, and every unrecognised shape is a failed snapshot with a reason rather than an invented gauge. Copilot stops being meterless: the seat pool becomes `included` and an `ai_credits` budget becomes `on-demand`, both derived from payloads the provider already fetched. That matters beyond the screen, because an empty meter list short-circuits admission to Unknown, so copilot had contributed nothing to the dispatch gate after a full day of real Copilot work. A saturated cursor or copilot meter now holds its own jobs the way a saturated claude meter does. Copilot's meter id moved from `ai-credits` to `included` to match cursor, so an operator who had pinned that chip re-pins it in Settings.
- **The model field is open on every harness.** All four schemas accepted a closed enum and now accept any non-empty slug, so `claude-fable-6` validates and round-trips the day the vendor ships it. Only an empty string is refused, since that is a caller who built the field from an unset variable. Each harness validates its own slug and does it better, answering an unknown model by naming its own catalog; what the enum bought was a toryo release on the one axis an operator most wants to move quickly. The lists survive as offered sets, still driving every picker and still the key type behind each rate table, so adding a model without pricing it is a compile error. `claude-fable-5-1` joins with its own row rather than Fable 5's, same input and output rates but a published cache read of $0.25 against Fable 5's $1.00, and cache reads dominate an agentic session. An unpriced model now costs the provider's rate ceiling instead of nothing, so every session on all four harnesses carries a cost and never a zero an operator would read as a free run. New `toryo-foreman models` asks each installed harness what it can run and names the drift in both directions. Claude publishes no catalog command, which is the finding the open field rests on rather than a gap in the report. Two surfaces stay curated on purpose, `toryo-completion --model` and board's task form, each to widen as its own contract change.
- **The harness and model picker is two dependent selects.** A per-role picker used to render the whole harness-by-model cross product in one list, five times over. A new `harness-model` render hint draws a harness select plus a model select over the same enum, and an object with several such fields grows an "All roles" setter above them, each role still individually overridable. Both lists come from the enum, so a pair the enum omits cannot be picked. A payload naming a retired slug, which is what a re-run seeded from an old run carries, renders a disabled option reading `(unavailable)` or `(unknown)` instead of a blank select over a value the form would still submit.
- **Idea impact is read from the idea.** It was recurrence times recency, arithmetic over how often a row had been re-filed and how recently, which never read a word of the idea. Against the live registry that left 492 of 618 scored rows inside one 0.05-wide band with a ceiling of 0.6, so the axis ordered nothing. Triage now estimates impact the way it already estimated effort, a local model reading the prompt text in batches against the five-band rubric, filled once and never re-scored over an operator's own judgment. `toryo-ideas triage --rescore-impact` is the one-time backfill of what the arithmetic wrote, and it is refused three times over on an operator-set score. The stored number is now a property of the idea rather than of the clock: the same idea scored on two different nights gets the same value, and board's impact-per-effort ordering changes with no code change.
- **Library search answers with sections.** Documents stay the unit you read, edit and export, but search now derives bounded sections from headings, ranks those, and returns the strongest section per document. A result carries its heading path, its position and a snippet, and omits the parent body, so a search answer stops spending context on documents you did not ask to read. Fetch the parent id with `get` when you want the whole source. The migration backfills one searchable fallback per existing document and `reembed` replaces those with real sections, so an existing library keeps answering while it upgrades.
- **Dispatch and sequence can answer how the last week went.** `toryo-dispatch history --since` reports terminal counts, a reliability ratio over successes plus failures, recovery attempts, stalled and capability-refused failures, policy denials, and how much of the log it could actually read. `toryo-sequence history --since` reports terminal runs, how many had repeats, and the executions beyond the first. The two are deliberately separate: sequence owns logical retries and resumes, dispatch owns in-place recovery, and none of the overlapping signals should be added together. Board draws both as one collapsed signals panel and marks only the owning section unavailable when an older installed daemon lacks the command. Capability refusal also gains its own error reason, so it stops being indistinguishable from a spawn failure.
- **foreman can say a service is starting.** `green` is a boolean, so a daemon that had taken its lock but not yet completed a healthy tick looked exactly like one nobody had launched, and board drew both as a red dot. Each probed service now carries a `state` of running, starting, unhealthy or down, derived from what the probe already knew. `up` no longer bounces a service that is mid-launch: it waits out that service's own window and reports it in a new `adopted` bucket, which matters because starting a service reaps orphans by signalling every matching process. Board polls once a second while anything is converging, draws a starting service yellow, and keeps Refresh live, since reading is not a transition. A pglite server that is up with unready databases is now dated from the PID it reports, so it reads as starting rather than as down. The overall verdict stays two-valued, so no exit code moves.
- **Relay serves a health route, which finishes the fast startup tier.** Waiting for a service to come green spawned the full daemon CLI probe every 500 milliseconds, about 110 milliseconds idle and 290 under load, for the whole of a boot that foreman could not see into. The four HTTP daemons already answered `/healthz` in about 0.2 milliseconds, and relay, the one daemon with no HTTP server, now does too. It is a tier and not a swap: the cheap route may only advance a wait, the full probe alone decides green, and a daemon serving HTTP with a wedged tick loop stays red exactly as before.
- **Board keeps you on the screen the work is on.** Ideas shows the live verification runs it started, each finished one's closed, proposed, unresolved and failed counts, marks the covered rows Verifying, and excludes them from the next sweep, rather than toasting once and leaving a long paid run visible only from the Sequence screen. The worker feed collapses capability declarations into one neutral summary that separates emulated support from a capability the job never used, with the raw event history still one click away. Re-pin is offered on a paused run as well as a failed one, and it probes without force first, so only a refusal naming `--force` opens a two-click confirmation carrying that refusal as its warning.
- **`toryo mcp list --json` emits `cursorDeeplink`.** Cursor is the only client toryo targets that publishes a one-click install URL, so a consumer wanting an "Add to Cursor" button no longer has to know the format or encode the entry. It is emitted whether or not this machine has Cursor, because the link is a property of toryo's entry. One caveat: it encodes this machine's entry, so from a source checkout it names that checkout and installs nothing useful elsewhere.
- **A release can be rehearsed.** `bun run release --rehearse` runs preflight, linux, build and e2e against whatever version is already named, writes into its own directory, keeps no state, and structurally refuses every stage that edits the tree or leaves the machine. Those gates only ever ran during a real cut, and every automated test run happens in a pristine worktree, so drift on the operator's own checkout used to surface mid-release. It now runs nightly on a self-hosted runner. A quiet-machine preflight check asks in the first minute what the install gate used to answer after the forty-minute build, namely whether this machine's own live stack will contaminate the run.
- **The hosted and public side.** The portal has a signed-in sidebar shell, admin's tenant console is reshaped, and each seat machine now reports the toryo version it has installed, so a machine running behind is visible rather than inferred. The marketing site names the coding agents toryo supports, collapses its changelog by release, and links reciprocally with the docs site, which now documents the Cursor gauges.

### Changed

- **Which project a knowledge call is about is now on the call.** `TORYO_BRAIN_PROJECT` and its matching request header are removed and setting either is inert. The pin was ambient and unvalidated: nothing resolved it, so a stale or mistyped value produced reads that quietly returned nothing and writes filed under an id naming no project, and it silently switched write semantics, since remembering defaulted to project scope when pinned and global when not. Reads take an optional `project` as a UUID or slug and every response states the scope it actually ran at, so an unscoped answer is visible rather than merely short. `code_search` requires one, because there is no global index to degrade to. Writes require a scope, and a project alongside project scope, with no default in either direction. A ref that resolves to nothing is an error naming it and never a silent fall back to global. Claude Desktop, which has no meaningful cwd and so could reach nothing but global, works now. A worker gets the ref through a "this session's project" block in its session context, since its working directory is a worktree no registered project contains. The control-plane tools lose their cwd fallback in the same move: an omitted project means every project on a list tool and a refusal on `dispatch_enqueue`.
- **The reviewer grades the work, not the builder's account of it.** `code-task`'s review prompt rendered the implementer's freeform hand-off, which mixes checkable gate facts with the implementer's own rationale. The hand-off now splits: a `gateAttestation` carries which gate commands ran and what they reported and is the only half the reviewer sees, while the hand-off keeps its name and its meaning and reaches the operator, the merge gate and the run record.
- **Library `add` and `update` return a receipt rather than the stored row.** It carries what was stored, the document id, title, scope, project, category, format and the body's byte count. Pass the id to `get` when you need the body back. Storage is unchanged: the complete body is persisted before the receipt is written.
- **A worker declares degraded capabilities only for what its payload can exercise.** Startup used to announce the provider's whole non-native matrix, including features the job had no way to request. Consumers that rebuilt a capability matrix out of those events now receive fewer and should read the capability map instead. Unsupported hard requirements still refuse the session before the provider starts.

### Fixed

- **A read-only Cursor session both runs and stays read-only.** Two defects, in opposite directions. The `--force` flag was dropped for read-only orientations on the reasoning that the deny set decides everything anyway, which is true of the flag alone and false beside the config toryo ships with it: an allowlist that is deliberately empty permits nothing, so every shell and MCP call was refused. Measured on a planner job, `pwd && ls` was refused while matching no deny rule. The session did not fail. It fell back to reading and grepping and produced a plan it could not verify, which is the quiet version of the bug, and Cursor was usable only for implementing. Meanwhile the deny set named tools and never covered a shell command that wrote without naming one, so a redirection from a reviewer created a file. A shell hook now judges redirection and tee by target: refused when the write lands in the repository under review, allowed outside it, which is the invariant the orientation actually states. That distinction is load-bearing, because a planner is required to write its own artifacts and redirection is the only route it has. Destructive verbs are refused everywhere, an unreadable target fails closed, and a guard that crashes blocks rather than waving through. Verified against the live CLI: read commands ran, and redirection, a checkout and a remove were each refused with nothing created.
- **`foreman restart dispatch --force` recovers a dispatch whose tick is dead.** The force-stop gate decided on the in-flight job count alone, so a wedged dispatch whose frozen running rows can never drain vetoed the very restart that would clear them. On 2 September that cost the stack two healthy dependents: dispatch reported a tick 424710ms stale against a 15000ms threshold with three jobs in flight, the gate declined, the stop half failed, and only a manual kill cleared it. The gate now reads the tick object already travelling in the same health response. A non-zero count is evidence of live work only while the tick is progressing, and past eight times dispatch's own self-tuning threshold it is a frozen snapshot that can never fall. Every uncertainty still declines, including an unreadable probe, a missing process id, an unknown count and a daemon that has never ticked, and a genuinely draining dispatch still declines too.
- **A run rooted with `--working-dir` carries its project.** A project was stamped only from `--project`, so a run started inside a registered repository was created project-less and every worker it dispatched got an unpinned knowledge server: project-scoped remembering, code search and directives were all refused for the whole run, while the reflect step still reported success. The working directory is now back-resolved against the project registry at run creation, which is the one moment the repository path is on the row. `--project` still wins, a registry failure degrades to an unpinned run rather than blocking one, and both outcomes are reported on stderr, because the incident's whole cost was its silence. The same row supplies the root scanned for a sequence file, so a run inside a project that forked a sequence now resolves that fork.
- **A required JSON artifact is checked where it is written.** A success check could assert only that a file existed, so a hand-off that was malformed, wrapped in prose or missing a field passed the worker and failed a later transform. Retry re-arms the run's latest step, so that transform re-read the same bad file forever and the only exit was writing the artifact by hand. `code-task`'s three JSON hand-offs now gate on a schema at the producer, so a bad artifact fails the worker that can rewrite it, and the diagnostics name the resolved path and the parse location without echoing the artifact's values.
- **The auto-injected memory block says what it left out.** Recalled project memories were filtered by an importance floor and rendered under a heading that read as the whole list, so a session could not tell a partial block from a complete one. It now names the dropped count, the floor as the reason, and the recall tool as the way to reach the rest.
- **A failed rescore no longer trades a content score back for arithmetic.** The impact fill fell back to recurrence whenever the model did not name a row, including on the rescore path where the row already carried a score, so one batch that timed out on every retry was counted and reported as rescored. The fallback now applies only where nothing is stored, so a rescore whose model was down changes nothing.
- **A database read error keeps its cause.** Nested driver errors were flattened into a generic message on the way out of dispatch and project reads, which is exactly where the message matters.
- **The release path reports its own failures.** A named preflight failure now carries the assertion block above it, so a gate that fails on a number the run already computed stops discarding that number and costing several round trips to a machine nobody sits at. Container base images are warmed by the build itself rather than only by CI, because a cold cache reads as a registry that is unreachable when it is merely slower than buildkit's deadline, once costing 56 minutes and a dead run. The rustup hint is quoted, since zsh expands a bare leading equals and the hint is the first command an operator pastes on a new runner. The nightly rehearsal gets full history, its checkout action is current, and a quiet-machine probe that fails open now raises a warning and a job summary rather than one indented line inside a 100-minute green log. A format gate that asserted a file count against the live working tree is gone, since it passed on every developer checkout and reddened on the loaded runner. And the dmg is styled again.
